correctness.rationale: The unital quotient has the 15 basis words of degrees 0 to 3. Its scalar and cubic coefficients contribute a 9-dimensional central factor. For v != 0 in the two-dimensional linear component, choose a basis with v=x: commutation with quadratic words gives 3 independent cubic images, and the linear-to-quadratic block adds 1 independent image; the kernel of that degree-two block contributes only a cubic image already counted. Hence rank(ad_a)=4 independent of Q and of characteristic. For v=0, only the map V -> V^⊗3, w |-> [Q,w], survives. A nonzero Q commutes with a nonzero w exactly when Q is a scalar w⊗w (five distinct word coefficients), so ranks 1 or 2 occur according to the quadratic Veronese locus. The q+1 projective lines w give q^2-1 nonzero Q tensors, yielding counts [q^9,(q^2-1)q^9,(q^4-q^2)q^9,0,(q^2-1)q^13] for ranks 0,1,2,3,4, summing to q^15. Averaging q^(15-r) centralizer sizes produces 2q^-4+q^-5-q^-6-q^-7. Independently enumerated every q^6 parameter pattern and computed full 15x15 commutator-matrix rank for q=2 and q=3, obtaining [1,3,12,48] and [1,8,72,648] before the q^9 factor. Those are finite corroborations, not the proof for all prime powers.
